title: J012--Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service
description: 1. Title: Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service 2. Background: Per NFPA 96, the new Food Services Center (Bldg. 211), and JLM dietetics are required to have their kitchen hoods cleaned semiannually due to limited grease use and/or limited meal service. The hoods for JLM, B170, and 202 require quarterly cleaning due to the heavy grease operations. During regular cleaning, the hood system must be inspected, tested and maintained. Per NFPA and regulatory requirements, kitchen fire suppression systems shall be inspected and serviced at a minimum of every 6 months to ensure proper operation and life safety compliance. Given that the kitchen fire suppression systems will be inspected, government is including the inspection, testing and maintenance of the portable fire extinguisher. Per NFPA and regulatory requirements, portable fire extinguishers shall be inspected, serviced, and hydrotested to ensure proper operation. 3. Purpose: The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16, located at Galleria Financial Center, 5075 Westheimer Rd, Ste 750, Houston, TX 77030, hereby issues the following Sources Sought to Request Information (RFI) with the intent of determining the contractor interest, capabilities, qualifications of potential businesses and estimated industry pricing information for market research and estimated budgetary purpose for Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning, Kitchen Fire Suppression System Service, and Portable Fire Extinguisher Service 4. Requirement summary: The Government presently considers fire-protection equipment inspection, testing, preventive maintenance, recharge, hydrostatic testing, repair, authorized replacement, and restoration to be the predominant purpose of the integrated requirement. Accordingly, North American Industry Classification System code 811310 is proposed.� The anticipated requirement combines recurring commercial services at the John L. McClellan Memorial Veterans Hospital in Little Rock and the Eugene J. Towbin Healthcare Center in North Little Rock. The draft scope includes:� Quarterly and semiannual cleaning of identified commercial kitchen hoods, plenums, ducts, fans, dampers, and related exhaust-system components.� Semiannual inspection, testing, maintenance, tagging, and documentation for 10 wet-chemical kitchen fire suppression systems.� Inspection, maintenance, recharge, hydrostatic testing, repair, authorized replacement, pickup, return, tagging, and asset-level reporting for approximately 948 portable fire extinguishers across listed classes and locations.� Qualified personnel, manufacturer authorization when required, calibrated test equipment, safety controls, chemical and waste management, impairment coordination, incident reporting support, and digital service records.� A potential base period with four one-year option periods. The final contract structure and quantities have not been determined.� Respondents should address the ability to perform all three principal service areas as the prime contractor and identify any anticipated subcontracting or teaming arrangement. 5. Requested capability information: Interested parties should submit a concise capability statement, preferably no more than 10 pages excluding cover page and supporting certifications. Clearly identify proprietary information. Address each item below in the order listed.� Legal business name, physical address, website, and primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address.� Unique Entity Identifier and Commercial and Government Entity code.� Business size under proposed North American Industry Classification System code 811310 and any recommended alternative code.� Socioeconomic status, including small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, women-owned small business, economically disadvantaged women-owned small business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone small business, 8(a) participant, or small disadvantaged business. Identify current Small Business Administration VetCert status when claiming veteran-owned or service-disabled veteran-owned status.� Whether the respondent intends to perform as the prime contractor and the approximate percentage of work the respondent expects to perform with its own employees.� Capability to provide all required service areas at both campuses, including after-hours kitchen exhaust cleaning and normal-business-hours fire protection services.� Current qualifications and certifications relevant to National Fire Protection Association Standards 10, 17A, and 96; Underwriters Laboratories 300-listed systems; Ansul and PyroChem systems; kitchen exhaust cleaning; extinguisher maintenance; and hydrostatic testing. Identify whether credentials are held by the respondent or a proposed subcontractor.� At least two recent and relevant contracts or projects completed within the past five years. Include customer, contract or project identifier if releasable, period of performance, dollar magnitude or range, scope, locations, and customer point of contact if authorized.� Available staffing, mobilization timeframe, service radius, emergency or impairment response capability, and ability to maintain recurring schedules at both campuses.� Quality-control approach, asset tracking, service-report format, deficiency management, chain-of-custody controls, and ability to provide searchable Microsoft Excel or Portable Document Format reports.� Any contract vehicle available to the Government, including Federal Supply Schedule contract information, if applicable.� 6. Licenses, certifications, and technical qualifications: Respondents shall identify the licenses, certifications, manufacturer authorizations, and technical qualifications currently available to perform the draft requirement. A credential matrix is acceptable at the Sources Sought stage. Do not submit Social Security numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, or other unnecessary personal information. Current Arkansas Fire Protection Licensing Board company Certificate of Registration for portable fire-extinguisher systems and fixed fire-suppression systems. Current individual Arkansas licenses for proposed or available technicians covering portable fire extinguishers, fixed wet-chemical fire-suppression systems, and hydrostatic testing, as applicable to assigned work. Current Ansul and Pyro-Chem manufacturer-authorized distributor, service-provider, or technician documentation applicable to the installed system models. Identify any other manufacturer authorization available. International Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Association Certified Exhaust Cleaning Specialist, Certified Exhaust Cleaning Technician, or an equivalent nationally recognized commercial kitchen exhaust-cleaning credential for the proposed crew leader or onsite supervisor. A Professional Exhaust Cleaning Technician designation should be identified as a designation rather than represented as a full certification. Current Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration Requalifier Identification Number approval for any facility that will inspect, test, mark, or requalify regulated cylinders. If this work will be subcontracted, identify the proposed testing facility and provide its approval information. Current Arkansas hydrostatic-testing license or certificate applicable to the cylinder classes and testing methods proposed. Current calibration certificates for pressure gauges, scales, hydrostatic-test equipment, electrical test instruments, and other measurement equipment whose accuracy affects inspection or acceptance. Relevant safety-training records, including lockout/tagout, hazard communication, personal protective equipment, fall protection or rooftop work, ladder or lift operation, respiratory protection when applicable, and spill response. Current certificate of general liability insurance and identification of workers compensation and automobile

title: Sources Sought for FY26 Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway Maintenance Dredging ????????? Select Sites
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. The Savannah District Corps of Engineers is requesting information regarding the market capabilities of potential contractors that can perform maintenance and unclassified dredging on the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway (AIWW) sections of waterway Hell Gate and Florida Passage in Chatham County Georgia and Fields Cut in Jasper County South Carolina. This request does not obligate the Government in any way to post a Request for Proposal or award a contract. Information received will be considered for the purpose of market research and determining how to best move forward with the procurement. Applicable NAICS code is 237990 with a size standard of $45.0M. The potential magnitude for this requirement is estimated to be between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. The FY26 Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway (AIWW) maintenance dredging contract provides construction services, including furnishing personnel, transportation, mobilization and demobilization, equipment and materials required in connection with maintenance dredging and incidental related work. This contract is traditionally performed with a hydraulic cutterhead dredge, but other methods will be considered. The duration is expected to be five months (165 days) from Notice to Proceed. The Savannah Districts area of responsibility (AOR) of the federally maintained channel in the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway begins in Port Royal Sound, South Carolina and ends in Cumberland Sound, Georgia. The shallow draft federally maintained channel is twelve (12) feet deep MLLW with widths from ninety (90) feet in land cuts and one hundred fifty (150) feet in natural waterways. Savannah Districts FY26 AIWW maintenance dredging work is located within the state of Georgia (Chatham County) and in the state of South Carolina (Jasper County). The Hell Gate section of waterway is to be dredged to authorized width of 150 feet and depth of 12 feet. The work also includes options to dredge the Florida Passage and the Fields Cut sections of the waterway to authorized width of 150 feet and depth of 12 feet. Approximately two hundred thousand (200,000) cubic yards of maintenance material is anticipated to be removed from the Hell Gate section of the federally maintained channel in the waterway. Approximately fifteen thousand (15,000) cubic yards of maintenance material is anticipated to be removed from the Florida Passage section of the federally maintained channel in the waterway. Approximately fifty thousand (50,000) cubic yards of maintenance material is anticipated to be removed from the Fields Cut section of the federally maintained channel in the waterway. Sediment dredged from Hell Gate may be pumped approximately four (4) miles to a Beneficial Use placement site in tidal flats east of Ogeechee Bar. Sediment dredged from Florida Passage may be pumped approximately nine (9) miles to the Beneficial Use placement site in the tidal flats east of Ogeechee Bar. Sediment dredged from Fields Cut will be pumped to the adjacent confined upland containment area DMCA 14B. The attached Request for Information should be filled out and loaded via PIEE before the sources sought close on 20 November 2026, 11:00 a.m. (EST). Any questions should be emailed to the Contract Specialist, Rohan Bryan at Rohan.A.Bryan@usace.army.mil or Contracting Officer, Preston Jones at Preston.E.Jones@usace.army.mil.

title: MQ-4C Air Conditioner A_M32C-23A
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, Lakehurst, intends to solicit, negotiate and make an award on a Limited Competitive basis with OSHKOSH AEROTECH, LLC, CAGE: 54077 and their authorized distributors for the procurement of the C-23A LAND BASED AIR CONDITIONER, Part Number (P/N) L100000.C for the MQ-4C Triton Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Program in support of the United States Navy (USN). This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of (FAR) 12.102(a), which states that states decisions to restrict competition for acquisitions valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold (SAT), document the decision that only one source is available and the basis for the decision. The intended source is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or an authorized distributor of the required equipment. The OEM has stated that it is the sole manufacturer and has authorized distributors for this product line and owns all proprietary rights to the drawings, design, and manufacturing data. These data rights are not owned by the Government and cannot be purchased. Procuring an alternative product would result in unacceptable schedule delays that would negatively impact fleet readiness and effectiveness. Any alternate Land Based Air Conditioner that has not already been validated and verified for compatible use on the MQ-4C airframe would require extensive test and evaluation, a new validation certification, and significant engineering efforts. New operation training, Supply and Provisioning Support, Aircraft maintenance publications, Support Equipment operation and repair manuals will need to be updated/created to logistically support a new Air Conditioner. title: Sources Sought - Cross-Domain Capabilities
description: The U.S. Army Product Manager Communications Security (PdM COMSEC) is conducting market research and technical requirements refinement to identify mature commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS), government-off-the-shelf (GOTS), and near-term developmental cross-domain solutions. To support next-generation enterprise and forward tactical architectures, proposed capabilities must align with National Cross Domain Strategy and Management Office (NCDSMO) "Raise the Bar" (RTB) 5.1 or newer guidelines. The Government requires robust, policy-enforced information exchange across disparate operational boundaries, spanning fixed enterprise data centers, vehicle-mounted systems, and expeditionary edge nodes subject to strict Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) constraints, as well as commercial and government cloud infrastructures up to Impact Levels 5 and 6 (IL5/IL6). Operationally, the requested cross-domain capabilities must maintain secure, line-rate data transfers across diverse security classification domains�ranging from Unclassified and Secret and Below (SAB) to higher security enclaves�while bridging High Threat Networks (HTN), Internet-accessible segments, and key multinational mission partner feeds. This includes interoperability across Five Eyes (FVEY) networks, Combined Joint All-Domain Command and Control (CJADC2) federations, and coalition partners. Feedback gathered from this RFI will be utilized by Army leadership to evaluate market readiness, validate integration feasibility, identify cyber and supply chain vulnerabilities, and establish procurement and programmatic milestones for upcoming contract acquisitions.

This notice is a market research tool and has not been set-aside for any small business category, but the notice is issued to determine appropriate set-aside categories. Responses to this notice, in conjunction with other Government market research resources, will be used by the contracting officer to determine the applicable socio-economic set-aside for the procurement. Failure to respond to this notice will not impact consideration of architect and engineer firms (or joint ventures) which otherwise meet set-aside requirements and submit responses to the follow-up public announcement. Once the appropriate set-aside is determined, a separate public announcement requesting qualification statements (SF330s) will be publicized on Contract Opportunities in accordance with 40 U.S. Code § 1101 and FAR 36.102. General Project Description and NAICS Synopsis of required services (See attachment for full statement of work): provide Architect/Engineer (AE) services to evaluate existing conditions, propose corrective measures, and design a construction project at the VA Maine Health Care System (Togus) in accordance with this scope of work. Scope will include Type A services only with design complete to 35%. AE Part I Investigative Services/Schematic Design/Other Related Services shall include site visits, field investigation, studies and user interviews to prepare drawings, and cost estimates for all facets of work and disciplines/trades to repair Chiller 3 to a condition where it will operate as designed. Design should also include fixes for the reported cooling and oil leaks. This procurement for Architect & Engineering services is assigned NAICS 541330 Engineering Services which has a SBA size standard of $22.5 million in average revenue. Information Sought The Government requests a letter of interest (or similar document) with responses to the following: 1. State your firm name (as it appears in SAM.gov), Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, and socio-economic status of the firm (i.e. verified SDVOSB, WOSB, SB, large business). 2. Provide a brief narrative on the firm s experience, providing services similar to those described in the attached statement of work. 3. What would be the expected make-up of the firm s team in terms of socio-economic categories and estimated percentage of work to be completed by your firm and each subcontractor? If the procurement is set-aside for any category of small business, generally fifty percent of more of the work would need to be performed by the contractor or a similarly situated subcontractor in terms of percentage of cost. For instance, if set-aside for service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB), 50% or more of the contract would need to be performed by verified SDVOSBs no other small business categories would count towards the percentage. If set-aside for small business, 50% of the contract would be required to be performed by small businesses which would include performance by a verified SDVOSB because they are also a small business. If the procurement is not set-aside and reaches certain dollar thresholds, the Government would negotiate an acceptable subcontracting plan to utilize small business concerns. 4. A brief statement of overall interest in the project and capability of performing the work in conjunction with ongoing projects. 5. Any additional capabilities statements or other documentation that you feel will assist the Government in performing market research and determining the appropriate set-aside. Submission Instructions Interested parties are requested to submit the requested information not later than November 20, 2026, to Diane C. Davis via email to diane.davis2@va.gov. title: Prototype development for Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination
description: This RPP is being issued by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), in support of the Defense Health Agency�s Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Medical Products (MP) Warfighter Protection (WPAC) & Acute Care Program Management Office (PMO) Care located in Frederick, Maryland at Fort Detrick. The Warfighter Protection and Acute Care Project Management Office (WPAC PMO) has a requirement for the development of a Barrier Combination product. The Barrier Combination product is defined as being composed of both a physical barrier to protect a wound and an antibacterial and/or antifungal activity released from the barrier to prevent the spread of organisms and avoid systemic infections. This RPP will result in one award to develop the Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination (BC) prototype product. The final product MUST be a combination wound treatment that includes a barrier component that is either infused or impregnated with antimicrobial and/or antifungal properties and have U.S. Food Drug Administration (FDA) approval (or clearance). The award, as a result of this RPP, will be awarded under the authority of prototype Other Transaction Authority (pOTA) 10 U.S.C. 4022. title: 30 RS Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST)
description: This requirement is for procurement of services including providing personnel, services, and management support for the Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST) software. The service will provide timely remote and periodic on-site support to the 30RS for MPST. The service includes maintaining compatibility with upgrades to the RQ-170 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware, and databases by utilizing improved and/or expanded intelligence products. It will also ensure the software accurately represents new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Provide software and database maintenance and support functions to the 30 RS for the Mission Planning Support Tools (MPST) and Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration and Modeling (AFSIM). The contractor shall provide software programming support for MPST computer program and its integration with AFSIM. All individuals performing on-site on this PWS must have a current adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, SAP information and associated ACCMs. Contractor personnel shall be conversant in the computer programming skills to fully support MPST, the version of AFSIM used by the RQ-170 simulator, be familiar with RQ-170 aircraft survivability, capabilities, Blue/Gray/Red ground and airborne threat systems, and Suppressor modeling capabilities/architecture/function/programming. Suppressor model may contain Foreign Government Information. The contractor shall provide support in training in the use of the version of AFSIM currently being used by the RQ-170. Actual work performance location is the contractor facility with periodic on-site visits to Creech AFB, NV and other classified locations as determined by the government.

title: Synthesis and Distribution of Drugs of Abuse and Related Compounds
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) whether commercials sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) Division of Therapeutics and Medical Consequences (DTMC) and National Institutes of Health (NIH) is seeking Capability Statements from business organizations with the demonstrated capability of providing service to support NIDA DTMC with the synthesis and distribution of drugs of abuse and related compounds. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) is seeking capability statements from businesses with the capability to synthesize and distribute drugs of abuse and related compounds. The NIDA Drug Supply Program has played an important role in promoting and supporting the substance use research by providing a wide variety of authentic, pure, controlled and uncontrolled drugs and other chemical compounds (both unlabeled and labeled with deuterium, tritium, carbon -14, and iodine-125 isotopes) to the drug abuse research community for basic research. To continue to supply authentic and pure drugs and research chemicals, NIDA maintains the drug supply inventory, periodically check chemical purity and supply to research investigators according to the NIDA drug supply guidelines. Specifically, NIDA plans to continue to: (1) produce, acquire, synthesize and maintain several radio and deuterium labeled and unlabeled drugs of abuse and other chemical substances in its drug supply inventory and distribute them to research investigators upon approval; (2) analyze, test, establish, and maintain the purity of drugs of abuse, and other chemical compounds in the NIDA drug supply inventory and produce updated chemical data sheets; (3) to replenish existing drug supply inventory with depleted drugs and research compounds with the synthesis or acquisition of depleted drug/chemical substances routinely; (4) to identify, acquire, and update the drug supply inventory with newly discovered chemical compounds useful for drug abuse research; (5) to use, maintain, and update the NIDA drug supply data base, known as Drug Inventory Supply Control System (DISCS); and (6) accept and process request packages from researchers; (7) Provide secure storage for all compounds and safe shipment of approved drugs/compounds to research investigators. Capable vendors must demonstrate the capability to receive the current inventory of hundreds of DEA controlled and uncontrolled drugs, other chemical compounds including peptides (opioid and related neuropeptides) in several kilogram quantities for immediate storage. Many of these compounds will require refrigeration. Some substances are in solution form and therefore require appropriate and secure storage to meet DEA requirements. Chemical compounds to be synthesized shall include new drugs, drug metabolites and other compounds as directed by NIDA. Specific compounds may include but not be limited to unlabeled compounds as well as compounds labeled with tritium, 125I, 14C, and deuterium and 13C. Representative classes of compounds shall include cannabinoids, hallucinogens, narcotics and antagonists, stimulants, depressants, peptides (opioid and related neuropeptides). All chemical compounds must be stored under optimum shelf?life conditions and their purity maintained at not less than 95%. Re-purification must be carried out if chemical or radiochemical deterioration occurs. MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS: To handle controlled substances under the Controlled Substances Act of 1970, it is mandatory that the successful capable vendors possess a DEA Research Registration for Schedules II to V and demonstrate the capability to obtain a DEA registration for Schedule I controlled substances. INSTRUCTIONS: Based on preliminary market research, the Government has determined that the requirements described herein do not meet the definition of a commercial product or commercial service as defined in RFO 2.101, and therefore, RFO Part 12 procedures are not applicable to this requirement. However, if a capable vendor believes that these services or products qualify as commercial under FAR 2.101, the vendor may submit a written justification for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Such submissions must be provided to the Contracting Officer no later than November 20, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. Respondents must provide clear and convincing documentation of their capability and experience with providing the personnel and services as specified in the tasks above. Also, information must be provided in sufficient details of the respondents� (a) staff expertise, including their availability, experience, formal and other training; (b) current capability to perform the work; (c) prior completed projects of similar nature; (d) corporate experience and other management capability; and (e) examples of prior completed Government contracts, references, and other related information. Each capability statement must include the respondent�s UEI number, organization name, and address. Each response should include the technical and administrative points of contact with, names, titles, addresses, telephone numbers, and e-mail addresses. The capability statement should clearly identify the size and type of business (e.g., 8(a), HubZone, Non-Profit, Other Than Small Business, etc.), pursuant to the applicable NAICS code and any other information that may be helpful in developing or finalizing the acquisition requirements. One (1) copy of the response is required and must be in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format using 11-point or 12-point font, 8-1/2� x 11� paper size, with 1� top, bottom, left and right margins, and with single or double spacing. The information submitted must be in an outline format that addresses each of the elements of the project requirement and in the capability statement paragraphs stated herein. A cover page and an executive summary may be included but is not required. The response is limited to ten (10) pages. The 10-page limit does not include the cover page, executive summary, resumes, or references, if requested. Any business concerns that believe they possess the capability necessary to successfully undertake the work described above must SUBMIT CAPABILITY STATEMENTS ELECTRONICALLY to the Contract Specialist, Shaun Rostad at Shaun.Rostad@nih.gov, NO LATER THAN 1:00 p.m. EST on November 20, 2026. title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

title: Synthesis and Distribution of Drugs of Abuse and Related Compounds
description: This is a SMALL BUSINESS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) whether commercials sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code 541715 should not submit a response to this notice. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method including small business socioeconomic set aside possibilities and to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) Division of Therapeutics and Medical Consequences (DTMC) and National Institutes of Health (NIH) is seeking Capability Statements from Small Business organizations with the demonstrated capability of providing service to support NIDA DTMC with the synthesis and distribution of drugs of abuse and related compounds. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) is seeking capability statements from small businesses with the capability to synthesize and distribute drugs of abuse and related compounds. The NIDA Drug Supply Program has played an important role in promoting and supporting the substance use research by providing a wide variety of authentic, pure, controlled and uncontrolled drugs and other chemical compounds (both unlabeled and labeled with deuterium, tritium, carbon -14, and iodine-125 isotopes) to the drug abuse research community for basic research. To continue to supply authentic and pure drugs and research chemicals, NIDA maintains the drug supply inventory, periodically check chemical purity and supply to research investigators according to the NIDA drug supply guidelines. Specifically, NIDA plans to continue to: (1) produce, acquire, synthesize and maintain several radio and deuterium labeled and unlabeled drugs of abuse and other chemical substances in its drug supply inventory and distribute them to research investigators upon approval; (2) analyze, test, establish, and maintain the purity of drugs of abuse, and other chemical compounds in the NIDA drug supply inventory and produce updated chemical data sheets; (3) to replenish existing drug supply inventory with depleted drugs and research compounds with the synthesis or acquisition of depleted drug/chemical substances routinely; (4) to identify, acquire, and update the drug supply inventory with newly discovered chemical compounds useful for drug abuse research; (5) to use, maintain, and update the NIDA drug supply data base, known as Drug Inventory Supply Control System (DISCS); and (6) accept and process request packages from researchers; (7) Provide secure storage for all compounds and safe shipment of approved drugs/compounds to research investigators. Capable vendors must demonstrate the capability to receive the current inventory of hundreds of DEA controlled and uncontrolled drugs, other chemical compounds including peptides (opioid and related neuropeptides) in several kilogram quantities for immediate storage. Many of these compounds will require refrigeration. Some substances are in solution form and therefore require appropriate and secure storage to meet DEA requirements. Chemical compounds to be synthesized shall include new drugs, drug metabolites and other compounds as directed by NIDA. Specific compounds may include but not be limited to unlabeled compounds as well as compounds labeled with tritium, 125I, 14C, and deuterium and 13C. Representative classes of compounds shall include cannabinoids, hallucinogens, narcotics and antagonists, stimulants, depressants, peptides (opioid and related neuropeptides). All chemical compounds must be stored under optimum shelf?life conditions and their purity maintained at not less than 95%. Re-purification must be carried out if chemical or radiochemical deterioration occurs. MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS: To handle controlled substances under the Controlled Substances Act of 1970, it is mandatory that the successful capable vendors possess a DEA Research Registration for Schedules II to V and demonstrate the capability to obtain a DEA registration for Schedule I controlled substances. INSTRUCTIONS: Based on preliminary market research, the Government has determined that the requirements described herein do not meet the definition of a commercial product or commercial service as defined in RFO 2.101, and therefore, RFO Part 12 procedures are not applicable to this requirement. However, if a capable vendor believes that these services or products qualify as commercial under FAR 2.101, the vendor may submit a written justification for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Such submissions must be provided to the Contracting Officer no later than November 20, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. Respondents must provide clear and convincing documentation of their capability and experience with providing the personnel and services as specified in the tasks above. Also, information must be provided in sufficient details of the respondents� (a) staff expertise, including their availability, experience, formal and other training; (b) current capability to perform the work; (c) prior completed projects of similar nature; (d) corporate experience and other management capability; and (e) examples of prior completed Government contracts, references, and other related information. Each capability statement must include the respondent�s UEI number, organization name, and address. Each response should include the technical and administrative points of contact with, names, titles, addresses, telephone numbers, and e-mail addresses. The capability statement should clearly identify the size and type of business (e.g., 8(a), HubZone, Non-Profit, Other Than Small Business, etc.), pursuant to the applicable NAICS code and any other information that may be helpful in developing or finalizing the acquisition requirements. One (1) copy of the response is required and must be in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format using 11-point or 12-point font, 8-1/2� x 11� paper size, with 1� top, bottom, left and right margins, and with single or double spacing. The information submitted must be in an outline format that addresses each of the elements of the project requirement and in the capability statement paragraphs stated herein. A cover page and an executive summary may be included but is not required. The response is limited to ten (10) pages. The 10-page limit does not include the cover page, executive summary, resumes, or references, if requested. title: 30 RS Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST)
description: This requirement is for procurement of services including providing personnel, services, and management support for the Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST) software. The service will provide timely remote and periodic on-site support to the 30RS for MPST. The service includes maintaining compatibility with upgrades to the RQ-170 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware, and databases by utilizing improved and/or expanded intelligence products. It will also ensure the software accurately represents new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Provide software and database maintenance and support functions to the 30 RS for the Mission Planning Support Tools (MPST) and Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration and Modeling (AFSIM). The contractor shall provide software programming support for MPST computer program and its integration with AFSIM. All individuals performing on-site on this PWS must have a current adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, SAP information and associated ACCMs. Contractor personnel shall be conversant in the computer programming skills to fully support MPST, the version of AFSIM used by the RQ-170 simulator, be familiar with RQ-170 aircraft survivability, capabilities, Blue/Gray/Red ground and airborne threat systems, and Suppressor modeling capabilities/architecture/function/programming. Suppressor model may contain Foreign Government Information. The contractor shall provide support in training in the use of the version of AFSIM currently being used by the RQ-170. Actual work performance location is the contractor facility with periodic on-site visits to Creech AFB, NV and other classified locations as determined by the government.

description: Request for Information (RFI) Department of the Navy (DON). Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY (as defined in FAR 15.101(c)); this is not a solicitation. A formal solicitation is not available at this time. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government and does not obligate the Government to award a contract or pay for the information provided in response. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. In accordance with FAR 15.101 (c), RFI, the Government does not currently intend to award a contract, but wants to obtain price, delivery, market, or capabilities information for planning purposes. Responses to RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. Information received in response to this RFI will be safeguarded adequately from unauthorized disclosure. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO THIS RFI Response Format/Page Limitations: As this is not a proposal the Government recommends a clear concise response and requests responses be limited to 25 pages or less. Interested parties should limit marketing material to allow for direct and substantive responses to the information requested by the Government. IMPORTANT NOTE: If your company has an existing contracting vehicle that can fulfill this need (e.g., GSA Schedule, NAVFAC MAC/MACC, or any other existing contract/Basic Ordering Agreement), please provide enough information in your response for the Government to analyze those resources to include points of contact, contract number/name, etc. Any responding contractor may respond to any number of questions posed in this RFI (items A-H below); a submission does not mandate a response to each question asked. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond. High-Level Scope of Work Hangar Procurement & Erection: Turnkey procurement, delivery, and complete erection of two (2) temporary, Relocatable Metal Building (RMB) hangars (approximately 40,000 SF clear interior space each), including hangar doors, exhaust ventilation systems, provisions for overhead crane support, fire protection/suppression, lightning protection, physical security, and relocatable administrative/support modular units. Civil & Structural Construction: Mass grading, site excavation, drainage, backfill, and construction of reinforced concrete foundation slabs (approximately 40,000 SF each) with associated strip/spread footings, perimeter walls, and specialized protective floor coatings/sealers. Airfield Pavements: Construction of heavy-duty aircraft access aprons, taxiways, towaways, tug pads, and administrative vehicle hardstands connecting to existing airfield networks. Approximate size of 62,000 SF. Utility Infrastructure & Site Improvements: Extension, connection, and rerouting of comprehensive site utilities (domestic water, sanitary sewer piping and manholes, storm drainage, natural gas, underground electrical conductors, duct banks, manholes, and oil/water separation) and airfield security fence relocation with a new Access Control Point (ACP). The purpose of this RFI is to gather market intelligence on acquisition vehicles, current construction costs, RMB manufacturing and delivery lead times, project phasing, and industry best practices for airfield construction projects. A. Company Information Required All responding sources must submit a response in accordance with the information provided below. Company Name and Address Point of Contact (Name, Phone Number, Email) Company Business Size and Status (e.g., Large, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB) Primary NAICS code(s) (e.g. 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction) SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC) available for this work B. Corporate Capabilities & Experience Vendors should address their specific capabilities in executing federal construction projects, specifically near an active airfield. Similar Experience: Provide two (2) to three (3) examples of similar commercial or federal RMB construction projects completed within the last seven (7) years. Highlight any work performed within close proximity of active airports/airfields. Federal Access: Confirm your firm�s capability to adhere to military installation security requirements and obtain DBIDS (Defense Biometric Identification System) credentials for personnel access at Naval Air Station (NAS) Jacksonville, FL. C. Cost Estimation & Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) The Government seeks Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimates strictly for budgetary planning and market research. Pricing submitted is non-binding. Based on standard industry practices for a facility of this type, please provide a ROM breakdown and address the following cost elements: Cost Element Provide cost breakdown in the following manner: Phased ROM Estimate 1. Phase 1 Base Bid: Hangar 1 and foundation, 41,540 SF airfield pavement and site improvements including utilities for a complete and usable facility. Phase 1 must be complete by DEC2028. 2. Phase 2 Option 1: Hangar 2 and foundation, 20,460 SF airfield pavement and site improvements including utilities for a complete and usable facility. Phase 2 must be completed by DEC2029. If Option 1 is awarded with Base Bid or before Base Bid completion construction for both phases can be parallel. D. Cost Drivers What do you anticipate being the most significant cost drivers for a temporary hangar project specifically located at NAS Jacksonville Florida? E. Market Volatility Are there current supply chain constraints, equipment shortages, or labor rate spikes in the Northeast Florida market that the Government should account for in its budgetary estimates? F. Value Engineering What commercial best practices or alternative methods could the Government incorporate into the final Statement of Work to safely lower the overall project cost and reduce construction duration? G. Schedule: How many calendar days would you estimate for a standard RMB project of this nature, factoring in standard Northeast Florida weather delays? H. Industry Feedback: Government-Provided Information To maximize competition and ensure accurate pricing in a future formal solicitation, the Government seeks to understand what specific data the industry requires. What specific documents, site data, or surveys does your firm need from the Government in a formal solicitation package to provide a highly accurate, firm-fixed-price proposal? (e.g., specific types of hazardous material surveys, utility disconnect maps, laydown area dimensions, historical as-built drawings, etc.) Point of Contact & Submission Responses are due no later than 2:00 PM Eastern Time, November 20, 2026, via email to Lindsay Betteridge at lindsay.e.betteridge.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson at aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil Please note "RFI Response: Temp Hangar NAS JAX; N6945027RTEMP" in the subject line of your response. Mark your response as "Proprietary Information" if the information is considered business sensitive. The email file size shall not exceed 10 MB.

title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. title: TR-143A TRANSDUCERS
description: ITEM DESCRIPTION - Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane (NSWC Crane) has a requirement to procure TR-143A Transducers, Part Number: 7146100-302. These transducers are utilized in the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem, supporting United States (U.S) Navy and United Kingdom (UK) Ballistic Missile Submarine Nuclear Powered submarines as part of the Navigation Subsystem Sonar. These transducers are used in coordination with TR-333 Hydrophones to receive signals from the ocean floor and to improve submarine launch accuracy. The transducers are manufactured items used as replacement assets during normal refit, replenish, and replacement operations for the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem and support U.S. Ohio and Columbia class submarines in addition to UK Vanguard and Dreadnought class submarines. The proposed contract action is for a two-year ordering period extension and ceiling increase, on contract N0016426DGP87, a firm-fixed-price, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity contract with a five-year ordering period. The contract is for supplies which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Massa Products Corporation, Hingham, MA 02043 (CAGE 88958), under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.103-1 (c) (2), only one responsible source. The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis, because the supplies have been deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on contract for the continued production of highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that award to any other source would result in (A) Substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition or (B) Unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Additionally, the Government is pursuing a sole source procurement to mitigate associated certification costs and certification testing that can take up to thirty-six months to complete. Furthermore, if a potential vendor is not capable of meeting the certification requirements, there is high likelihood that ship schedules will be significantly impacted. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract extension based upon responses to the solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of re-evaluating the justification for sole source or limitation of sources and making a determination to change the acquisition strategy to a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Questions or inquiries should be directed to Steven Junkins, Code 0232, e-mail steven.l.junkins2.civ@us.navy.mil. Please reference the above solicitation number when responding to this notice.

title: Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) fuel services at Naval Air Station Corpus Christi, TX
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice/Synopsis - Naval Air Station (NAS) Corpus Christi, Texas, SPE603-27-R-5X03 Government Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft and Ground Fuel Services, Bulk Fuel Storage and Distribution Services at NAS Corpus Christi, TX. This is a Pre-solicitation Notice to Sources Sought Notice posted under SPE603-26-R-5X20. This Pre-solicitation notice SPE603-27-R-5X03 is for GOCO services at NAS Corpus Christi, TX. Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy-FESAB will be issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for fuel services to include all personnel, equipment, vehicles, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform aircraft and ground fuel support services at NAS Corpus Christi, TX. The contractor shall be responsible for a comprehensive range of fuel-related services. This includes the management, operation, maintenance, product quality surveillance, inventory and accounting controls, security, safety, and environmental protection of the assets, properties, and performance duties as identified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The contractor�s duties shall encompass the following: Fuel Operations: Receiving, storing, testing, and issuing aviation and ground fuels. Bulk Fuel Storage: Managing two 6,000-barrel aboveground fuel storage tanks and associated infrastructure. Fuel Servicing: Providing mobile refueling and defueling services for aircraft, including support for outlying fields (NOLF Cabaniss, NOLF Waldron, and NOLF Goliad on an emergency basis). Ground Fuel Services: Operating and maintaining the base service station, which dispenses unleaded and diesel fuel. Quality Surveillance: Ensuring fuel products meet all required specifications through sampling, testing, and laboratory operations. Maintenance: Performing operator-level maintenance on all government-furnished equipment and facilities. Safety and Environmental Compliance: Adhering to all applicable Department of Defense (DoD), federal, state, and local regulations. The contractor will be required to: Provide all necessary personnel, equipment, and supplies to perform the services outlined in the PWS. Develop and submit detailed plans for contract compliance, quality control, maintenance, staffing, and safety. Utilize a contractor-furnished Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to track and report on all maintenance activities. Meet all performance requirements and be subject to quality assurance monitoring by the government. Ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. Provide 24/7 fuel dispatch services and be prepared to support unscheduled and emergency fueling requirements. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage), and the size standard is $36.5 million. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2031), a five-year option period (April 1, 2031 through March 31, 2036), and an option to extend the contract for up to six one-month periods (April 1, 2036 through September 30, 2036). DLA Energy is working towards posting the solicitation in the November � December 2026 timeframe. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Dates of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the site visits, will be listed in the solicitation. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: TACDS Services
description: Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Newport, has a requirement for fleet installation and sparing for TACDS units. These TACDS units require battery replacement every five years, otherwise they will not be suitable for fleet use. The anticipated dollar amount is $44,800 for sixteen (16) TACDS units to be screened, have their batteries swapped, reset to factory settings, and corrected firmware updated. This effort will providea assets available to support anticipated demand. These TACDS units are supported on a Sole Source basis because only General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has the capability to replace existing batteries, complete the factory reset, and establish correct firmware. The TACDS units created by GDMS have been shock tested in the cabinets and is therefore the only unit approved for use in the existing platform. The design, development and environmental qualification efforts associated with an alternate would be cost prohibitive for the overall program. Furthermore, the requalification process would be detrimental to the overall program. Based on the above, it is not reasonable to conclude the potential savings from competition can offset the duplicative cost and schedule/mission impact associated with purchasing a new brand name product. Therefore, it is in the best interest of the government to solicit this requirement on brand name only basis. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals; however, any interested party that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation. The Government will consider all responses received within the posting period as market research. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. title: Design-Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood, TX
description: *****AMENDMENT 0003 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON MONDAY, 02 NOVEMBER 2026**** *****AMENDMENT 0002 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON MONDAY, 19 OCTOBER 2026**** *****AMENDMENT 0001 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON TUESDAY, 22 SEPTEMBER 2026***** Request for Proposal (RFP), Solicitation No. W912QR25RA013 is issued for the repair of a failing Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood (formerly Fort Cavazos), TX. This project will repair and construct an addition to an existing ~26,000 square feet of the maintenance part of the Equipment Concentration Site, Maintenance Building 56767, that is in a failing condition, and has not undergone any major infrastructure or system repairs, only limited maintenance and repair work has occurred. The project includes repair of HVAC and Electrical systems, remove non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspace, restore inadequate and non-code compliant bathrooms, repair light fixtures with code compliant units, failed flooring, code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, repair electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided to include a code compliant entrance ramp. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. This project contains options. The contract duration is estimated at 913 calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed (NTP).This award is Subject to the Availability of Funds (SAF). TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: Total Small Business Set-Aside Procurement. SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase Design/Build procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best-Value Tradeoff (BVTO) source selection process. The technical information contained in each Offeror s proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Phase II Selected Offerors are requested to submit additional information described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, Schedule Narrative, and Price. The Standard Form (SF) 1442, resubmission of Evidence of Ability to Obtain Bonding and Proof of Financial Ability, and resubmission of Pre-Award Information will also be required. All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. NEGOTIATIONS: The Government intends to award without negotiations, but reserves the right to conduct negotiations should it be deemed in the Government s best interest. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The estimated construction magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS: Paper copies of the solicitation and amendments will not be issued. Telephone, email, and fax requests for this solicitation, amendments, and attachments (plans and specifications) will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To be able to download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the System for Award Management at https ://sam.gov. Amendments, when issued, will be posted to the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Portal and SAM.gov websites for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the websites periodically for any and all amendments to the solicitation. System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror .POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contact for this procurement is Bonny Dylewski, at bonny.c.dylewski@usace.army.mil. title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR SECURED JANITORIAL SERVICES AT MARINE CORPS BASE (MCB) QUANTICO, VA
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: Secured Janitorial Services. Marine Corps Base, Quantico, VA 22134-2134 SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR SECURED JANITORIAL SERVICES AT MARINE CORPS BASE (MCB) QUANTICO, VA. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington/Facilities, Engineering, and Acquisition Division (FEAD) Quantico is seeking Small Business Administration�s eligible certified 8(a) participants capable of performing secured janitorial services for Marine Corps Base Quantico, (MCBQ). THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL USED TO DETERMINE THE AVAILABILITY AND ADEQUACY OF POTENTIAL CERTIFIED 8(A) SOURCES PRIOR TO DETERMINING THE METHOD OF ACQUISITION AND ISSUANCE OF AN AWARD. THIS SURVEY IS FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. Respondents will not be notified of the evaluation. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. No telephone calls or emails will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement, if any, that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The appropriate NAICS Code is 561720, Janitorial Services, and the corresponding size Standard is $22.0 million. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by FEAD Quantico, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The intent of this notice is to identify potential Offerors for market research purposes. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to identify eligible certified 8(a) participants with the primary NAICS 561720, capacity, experience, and interest in the secured janitorial services for three secured buildings within the area of responsibility of Marine Corps Base Quantico, (MCBQ) VA. The secured janitorial recurring work is summarily described as: Provide all labor, supervision, management, coordination, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide janitorial services in various secured buildings at MCB Quantico. This requirement includes non-recurring work (also known as Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)) wherein task orders for pre-priced contract line items or negotiated labor and materials for services in excess of recurring services are issued. Interested sources shall demonstrate the experience and capability in the services described above, demonstrate the ability to transition to 100% operational capacity within 60 days or less, and the capability to provide secure janitorial staff. All work under the contract is performed in secure areas and all Contractor personnel requiring access to a secure area shall possess an active final Top Secret Facility Clearance (access to COMSEC and NATO) without any Special Limitations that restrict access. Interim clearances are not accepted for TS/SCI contract efforts. The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring all contract personnel are U.S. citizens and possess an in-scope (per current DoD 6-year reinvestigation requirement), favorable, Single Scope Background Investigation (SSBI) / T5 investigation (to include SBPR, PPR or T5R), or currently enrolled in the DoD Continuous Evaluation (CE) / Continuous Vetting (CV) program, adjudicated for Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) eligibility by the DoD Central Adjudication Facility (DoD CAF) without conditions, exceptions, or waivers at the time of award and prior to performance under this contract. The Contractor shall ensure it and any subcontractors have completed all DD Form 254 requirements prior to commencing any work under this contract. The request shall be renewed annually or for the duration of the contract if less than one year. If awarded, the contract will consist of a base period and four (4) one-year option periods. If, at the end of the contract term, the Government does not award a follow-on contract in time, the Government may require the Contractor to continue performance for an additional period of up to six months under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Clause 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services. In accordance with FAR Part 15, this project will be procured utilizing contracting by negotiations. All certified, eligible 8(a) participants capable of performing this work are encouraged to respond. Capabilities Statement Packets: It is requested that all responsible, interested certified 8(a) participants submit a capabilities statement package demonstrating ability to perform the requested services. The document must be no more than 3 pages in length, singled-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman font minimum, excluding title page. This documentation shall address, at a minimum, the following: (1) Company profile to include number of employees, office location(s), Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Cage Code, VETS 4212 Proof of Submission and a statement regarding small business designation and status and any certifications to the designation. (2) Relevant Experience of three (3) recent and completed projects. Details should include whether the concern was a prime or subcontractor, contract value, square footage and a brief description of the scope performed, contracting agency, contract number, title, place of performance, years of performance, value of contract per year, and any security requirements. The Government reserves the right to request additional information as needed from all respondents. The Statement of Capabilities package must be complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the NAVFAC team to determine the firm�s capabilities. Information submitted will only be considered for this sources sought. Responses, questions, or comments shall be emailed to Ms. Luz M. Baron, Contract Specialist Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: luz.m.baron.civ@us.navy.mil or Ms. Dotty M. Medel, Contract Specialist Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: dotty.m.medel.civ@us.navy.mil All responses must be received no later than November 20, 2026, at 2:00 PM EST. Submissions received after this deadline will not be evaluated. Only email responses will be entertained. Thank you for your interest and support of NAVFAC Washington and the Warfighter.

The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis, because the supplies have been deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on contract for the continued production of highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that award to any other source would result in (A) Substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition or (B) Unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Additionally, the Government is pursuing a sole source procurement to mitigate associated certification costs and delays required for certification testing. Furthermore, if a potential vendor is not capable of meeting the certification requirements, there is high likelihood that mission schedules will be significantly impacted.
