title: Parker Hannifin Sole Source Adds to LTC
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Aviation, Richmond proposes to issue a Letter Request for Proposal (RFP) to support a DLA Strategic Initiative. This strategic effort includes multiple NSNs to support various sole source weapon systems / operational platforms. A total of 153 NSNs for various platforms / weapon systems are targeted for this RFP and contract action. OEM Parker Hannifin Corporation (59211) has been identified as the approved source of supply for the listed items; therefore, the proposed action is intended to be awarded on a sole source basis to the OEM. It is anticipated that 153 items will be awarded and priced with lead-times as add-ons to the OEM's existing Long-Term Contracts (LTCs): Captains of Industry (COI) Supplier Capabilities Contract (SCC) SPE4AX-21-D-9402 for commercial items and SPE4AX-21-D-9403 for military unique items. It is the Government's intent to use a letter solicitation format to the sole source Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM); therefore, if a non-OEM source is interested in any of the NSNs, please notify the Contracting Officer prior to the synopsis closing date. These items have been identified as sole source; however, some items may have history showing awards to other than the OEM. Surplus dealers are also invited to respond to this synopsis. The response should include a completed surplus certificate, DLA Procurement Note C04, Government Surplus Property Material or adequate traceability documentation to show that the product is acceptable. (Note: DLA Procurement Note M05 Evaluation Factor for Unused Former Government Surplus Property, will apply and other Aviation sites will provide their equivalent surplus documentation, as applicable). Responses to this announcement from other than the OEM should identify items of interest and include evidence of ability to supply the items in accordance with the aforementioned acquisition strategy. In addition, respondents should identify the available quantities, prices, and lead-times. DLA will consider all such responses and may alter the acquisition strategy if purchase of existing surplus or newly manufactured inventory is in the best interest of the government. Responses to this announcement from other than the OEM are required by Thursday, November 19, 2026. A copy of the letter of interest should be forwarded to the contracting officer identified herein and SBA PCR (jamal.thomas@sba.gov). title: Construct Interim Remedial Action (IRA) for the Nelson Tunnel Superfund Site
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. This is not a solicitation and any offers received as a result of this pre-solicitation notice will not be accepted or evaluated. USACE Omaha District intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) solicitation W9128F27RA056 for the following action in November 2026 with the planned proposal due date in January 2027. ***PLEASE REFERENCE THE SITE VISIT INSTRUCTIONS IN THE ATTACHED DOCUMENT AND RESPOND NO LATER THAN THE DATE SHOWN. Project Title: Construct Interim Remedial Action (IRA) for the Nelson Tunnel Superfund Site Project Location: One mile north of the town of Creede in Mineral County, Colorado NAICS Code: 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction PSC Code: Y1LC - Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures Set-Asides: This solicitation will be issued unrestricted; both small and large businesses are encouraged to participate. Synopsis of Project: Construction Services for the Nelson Tunnel/Commodore Waste Rock Site (Nelson Tunnel Site or Site), the focus of the interim remedial action (IRA), consists of an abandoned underground hard rock mine and drainage tunnel with several shafts, crosscuts and drafts branching off the main tunnel. The remedial action objective of the RA is to reduce the likelihood of a large, uncontrolled release of mine-impacted water from mine pools impounded within the Nelson Tunnel. The selected alternative for the Nelson Tunnel Interim Record of Decision (IROD) is to construct a bypass adit that connects into Nelson Tunnel at a sufficient distance from the surface to allow for installation of a flow-through hydraulic bulkhead within Nelson Tunnel. The IROD selected remedy is Alternative 4, Drive New Adit to Intersect Nelson Tunnel, Tunnel Rehabilitation, Install Bulkhead in Nelson Tunnel and Flow Control Structure in Commodore 5 level and include the following remedial components. 1. Installation of a new adit south of Nelson Tunnel, to bypass the Nelson Tunnel Portal Pool. 2. Rehabilitation of Nelson Tunnel from the bypass adit connection to the location where bulkhead construction is planned. 3. Installation of a flow control bulkhead in Nelson Tunnel to protect against a sudden uncontrolled release through Nelson Tunnel.4. Installation of an accessible bulkhead flow control structure in the Commodore 5 level to protect against a sudden uncontrolled release through this level. Additional Information can be found at the following EPA website provided in the attachment.

title: Laboratory Capabilities to Test Railroad Tank Car Thermal Protection Systems (TPS)
description: Request for Information (RFI) only. Purpose This RFI seeks information regarding Laboratory Capabilities to perform pool and torch fire tests of Thermal Protection Systems (TPS) to the U.S. DOT Volpe Center. A qualified vendor must be capable of performing pool and torch fire tests as described in 49 CFR 179 Appendix B. The vendor should also be capable of performing light fabrication and/or assembly of test specimens for the aforementioned tests. Qualified vendors are requested to respond as detailed further below, which includes capability, small business classification, estimated lead time including any risks that may impact delivery, and any other industry concerns the government might consider before solicitation. The intent is to gather information to inform a possible future procurement or contract. Background The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) is conducting research into the performance of TPS for railroad tank cars. TPS are designed to delay or prevent the catastrophic release of hazardous materials from a railroad tank car exposed to fires that may result from train derailments. In the FRA�s planned research, test specimens of TPS are to be evaluated in simulated pool fire and torch fire conditions similar to those defined in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. The durations of the fire exposure would extend beyond the 100 minute pool fire and 30 minute torch fire duration specified in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. Pool fire test specimens are applied to a 1 foot by 1 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. Torch fire test specimens are applied to a 4 foot by 4 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. The Volpe Center is looking to perform a minimum of two (2) pool fire tests and two (2) torch fire tests for each TPS. The total number of TPS to be tested has not yet been determined. Although the tests will be similar to those defined in 49 CFR 179 Appendix B, this research may require some modifications to the test protocol including but not limited to additional instrumentation, data collection or varying of test parameters such as duration of the fire exposure. The Volpe Center is also looking for the capability to perform light fabrication of test specimens as detailed above. For examples of possible fabrication requirements, see https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/standards-rulemaking/hazmat/tank-car-thermal-protection-system-list Scope of Information Requested The U.S. DOT Volpe Center is seeking information from commercial testing laboratories, university laboratories, and other interested parties on their willingness, ability, and experience in conducting the simulated pool and torch fire testing planned for various tank car TPS. Descriptions of your facility�s pool and torch fire testing capabilities, including equipment, experience, capacity, resources and staff preparedness for testing tank car TPS. You are encouraged to submit publications of relevant past work. Descriptions of any laboratory accreditation or certification related to pool fire testing. Laboratory hourly rates, technical personnel rates, general facility and equipment usage charges, overhead and other expenses, etc. Descriptions of staff/facility/equipment availability, including any limitations on when fire testing may be conducted (e.g., blackout dates due to seasonal weather conditions) Information on any pre-test data or preliminary sample testing that may be required prior to a full-scale test. Information on your typical post-test laboratory analyses and report formats, and your ability to tailor report/data formats to customer requirements. Description of your facility�s fabrication and assembly capabilities, including: Cutting of 11 gauge steel sheet (0.1196 inches) Cutting of 0.625 inch steel plate Cutting of insulating materials that may generate hazardous airborne particulates such as fiberglass. Mixing and application of coatings to required specifications similar to examples on the PHMSA TPS list. What is the required lead time for fabrication of test specimens? Technical personnel rates, general facility and equipment usage charges, overhead and other expenses, etc. for fabrication of test specimens. Estimated time to conduct one simulated pool fire and one simulated torch fire test including setup, conduct of the test, cooldown, and teardown of test setup. Any other comments that can help the U.S. DOT Volpe Center better define the research scope and direction and ultimately yield technical data beneficial to both the government and industry are welcome. Responses should include the above as well as: Company information Name UEI Address POC information This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and is a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and possible issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation for bids, quotations, and proposals, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a competitive contract. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government.

title: Supply Thermal Protection Systems for Railroad Tank Cars
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. Purpose This RFI seeks information regarding providing Thermal Protection Systems (TPS) for railroad tank cars to the U.S. DOT Volpe Center. A qualified vendor must demonstrate they are able to provide either complete test specimens as detailed further below or sufficient materials to fabricate completed test specimens without the need for specialized facilities or techniques. Qualified vendors are requested to respond as detailed further below, which includes capability, small business classification, estimated lead time including any risks that may impact delivery, and any other industry concerns the government might consider before solicitation. The intent is to gather information to inform a possible future procurement or contract. Background The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) is conducting research into the performance of TPS for railroad tank cars. TPS are designed to delay or prevent the catastrophic release of hazardous materials from a railroad tank car exposed to fires that may result from train derailments. In the FRA�s planned research, test specimens of TPS are to be evaluated in simulated pool fire and torch fire conditions similar to those defined in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. The durations of the fire exposure would extend beyond the 100 minute pool fire and 30 minute torch fire duration specified in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. Pool fire test specimens are applied to a 1 foot by 1 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. Torch fire test specimens are applied to a 4 foot by 4 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. The Volpe Center is looking to procure a minimum of two (2) pool fire test specimens and two (2) torch fire test specimens for each TPS. Multiple TPS of different construction from the same vendor may be considered. The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) maintains a list of tank car TPS that have been tested and shown to comply with the requirements of Appendix B to 49 CFR Part 179. Inclusion on this list is not a requirement for a TPS to be used on a tank car. There is a preference of TPS that are currently on the PHMSA list and/or being used on tank cars, but other systems may be considered. Scope of Information Requested The U.S. DOT Volpe Center is seeking information from tank car thermal protection system manufacturers and/or vendors, on their willingness, ability, and requirements to provide the physical specimens as well as material and installation information needed to conduct the above fire testing research. Description of how the TPS is assembled. Example : 1 inch insulation � Brand XXX 1 inch fiberglass � generic 11 gauge steel jacket � generic 10 mils coating � Brand YYY, Component A and Component B in 1:1 volume ratio Include any relevant brand names or item numbers specific to this system. Also include any required surface preparation or other processing steps. Is the TPS currently used on railroad tank cars? If so, is it on the PHMSA approved list here: https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/standards-rulemaking/hazmat/tank-car-thermal-protection-system-list Are you capable of supplying fully assembled test specimens? If YES, do you require government furnished plates on which to apply the TPS? If NO, are you prepared to supply detailed instructions on fabrication, including any considerations for required equipment, cutting, bonding, forming, attachment, surface preparation, mixing, curing/drying or any other fabrication steps? What is the required lead time for either assembled test specimens or sufficient materials for third-party fabrication? Your willingness to sell TPS for this third-party testing effort. Availability and willingness to share any existing pool and/or torch fire testing data on the subject TPS, and any sensitivities or proprietary data protections that would be needed prior to sharing such information. Estimated prices of either assembled test specimens or sufficient materials for third party fabrication. Any other comments that can help the U.S. DOT Volpe Center better define the research scope and direction and ultimately yield technical data beneficial to both the government and industry are welcome. Responses should include the above as well as: Company information Name UEI Address POC information This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and is a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and possible issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation for bids, quotations, and proposals, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a competitive contract. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government.

title: Robins RAPID Construction OTA Progressive Design Build Fiber Replacement
description: FA8501-27-RAPID-CIRCUIT F1-170129-OTA Under the RAPID Umbrella Framework: RAPID Progressive Design-Build to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation UHHZ170129 Description The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation at Robins AFB, GA. The requirement includes replacement of all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout circuit F-01. This will include replacement and removal all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes. This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Purpose The purpose of this Area of Interest is to obtain commercially viable, safe, and schedule-credible solutions to design plans for and to perform the replacement of expired high-risk Circuit F01 cabling in order to prevent operational risk, mission delays, and compounding economic costs due to infrastructure failure at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The Government requires an integrated approach to address the design, removal of deteriorated cables and replacement with new cable in The Fowler Substation. The selected approach must provide a practical path to execute the work while minimizing disruption to aircraft operations and controlling construction, safety, environmental, and schedule risks. Project Background and Existing Conditions Circuit F-01 has surpassed its operational lifecycle, creating a high-probability risk for catastrophic failure. If the remaining aged portion is not replaced, the installation faces risk of emergency repair premiums and disruption to sustaining airfield infrastructure, supporting safe aircraft movement, installation readiness, and continued mission operations. The work area is slightly congested and impacted by various airfield operations. description: 1. VAAR 852.219-75 in the solicitation has box (iii), special trade construction contractors (75 percent), marked, while the requirement is coded J061 under NAICS 238210 and FAR 52.219-14 is also included. Please confirm that the 75 percent special trade limitation in box (iii) is the limitation that applies to this award. Confirmed. This requirement is solicited under NAICS 238210. The applicable limitation on subcontracting is VAAR 852.219-75(c)(iii), 75 percent for special trade construction contractors. Offeror must comply with that limitation and submit the signed certificate. 2. The SAM.gov notice shows no set-aside, while the solicitation includes VAAR 852.219-73 (total set-aside for certified SDVOSBs). Please confirm that this requirement is a total SDVOSB set-aside. Confirmed. This is a total SDVOSB set-aside per VAAR 852.219-73 and SF1449 Block 10. NCO 21 will update the SAM.gov notice to reflect the set-aside. Offerors must be certified SDVOSB in SBA Veteran Small Business Certification at time of offer. 3. Section B.1 states that invoices are submitted upon Government inspection and acceptance. Will VA accept two invoices, one after acceptance of field testing and one after acceptance of the coordination study and final report? Yes, the VA will take two invoices. Station/contracting will review these invoices for approval. 4. Amendment 0001 added Attachment C27, Single-Line Schematics. Please confirm whether C27 and the Facility Single Line Diagram together define the full quantities to be tested (MV switches, MV cable runs and vaults, liquid-filled and dry-type transformers, circuit breakers 225A and above, and feeders), or provide an equipment list with counts. Please also identify the buildings covered by "Day 12 + TBD, new facilities since 2017." In the past, a copy of 1-line diagrams was updated with color coding of each test component and a sheet with all quantiles and locations. This should be done to ensure vendor and FMS understands what scope is. 5. For the coordination study and arc flash analysis, is the 2024 study model available to the contractor, and in what software? Is there a required software platform and CAD version for the deliverables? Yes. However, I was just informed that our 2020 circuit breaker testing is the performed format which we can provide. 6. Must the coordination study and arc flash analysis be sealed by a Professional Engineer, and if so, must the engineer be licensed in Nevada? Yes engineering seal is required. No, it does not need to be Nevada. In the past, the previous vendor has had an engineer on staff who did this. 7. Please confirm that the five years of experience in the Contractor Requirements section is verified as a responsibility matter after quotes, and that the quote itself consists of price, the signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, amendment acknowledgments, and the items listed in FAR 52.212-1(a). Confirmed. Contractor Requirements Para 7.3 [5-year experience] will be evaluated as part of responsibility per FAR 9.104 after quotes, not as part of technical acceptability. For quote submission, see FAR 52.212-1(a) as supplemented by Addendum: price on B.2 Schedule, signed SF1449 Block 30 if required, acknowledgment of amendments per B.1 Para 4, signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, and proof of SDVOSB certification status. See also 52.212-3 if not in SAM. 8. Will VA facility electricians perform switching for the outages, and will VA provide temporary power or generator support where emergency branch equipment is de-energized? It is preferred that be in the vendor s scope of work. But verbiage should state that it will be done with Electrical supervisor or designee s authority at time of switching. Vendor should be responsible for the switching of the medium voltage system (25KV). This would be the P/Q switch in Boiler plant yard, medium voltage switches, and transformers in/on the facility down stream from the P/Q switch. VA electricians may assist with switching for 600 volts and less to aid in the testing. This must be arranged in the presented schedule to ensure proper VA staff is available. 9. What is the anticipated award date and the targeted notice-to-proceed window, so offerors can hold test crews for the night schedule? Anticipated award is within 2-3 weeks after the 11/9/2026 due date, subject to evaluations. NTP is intended ASAP after award per SOW 8.1. Offerors should plan to start coordination within 1 week of NTP. We will not require crews to be held prior to NTP. 10. Will a site visit be offered before the quote due date, and if so, will attendance be optional? VA high encourages site visits to visit equipment types, locations, and quantities. This has not been a bidding mandate to attend, but is encouraged. 11. Is there a deadline for questions, and will answers be issued by amendment? Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers that affect the SOW or terms will be issued by formal amendment to all offerors. Administrative clarifications may be answered by email. 12. The quote submission method and address, and the question deadline. Quotes shall be submitted by email to alex.arter@va.gov. Quotes are due November 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM Pacific Time. File size: split emails if over 20MB. Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers affecting SOW/terms/pricing will be issued by formal amendment. 13. Whether a site visit at the Ioannis A. Lougaris VAMC (Reno) will be held, and its date. A site visit is planned. Attendance will be optional. Date/time and meeting location will be issued by amendment once coordinated with Engineering. Offerors are encouraged to attend to verify existing conditions. No energized work will be performed during the site visit. 14. Breaker and feeder quantities by voltage class (LV/MV), and whether protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in scope. From the previous tests. There are: 11 MV Switches 10 MV Transformers 477 Circuit Breakers 570 Feeder Cables 27 LV Transformers Protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in the scope. The arc-flash label updates are to have their associated room numbers on them and must be done with professional engravings (i.e. no hand drawn labels). 15. Planned outage windows, and whether shutdowns must be after hours or on weekends. Yes. Per SOW 8.6, Electrical Testing shall be performed during Off Hours - 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM, weekends, and federal holidays. Photography work shall be performed during Normal Hours (Mon-Fri 6AM-6PM). The sequencing in SOW 8.1 shall be used as the basis for pricing. Final outage windows will be coordinated with the COR 2 weeks in advance per SOW 8.7 to minimize impact to patient care. 16. Required standard and deliverables (for example, NETA MTS and VHA Directive 1028 reporting). The required standard and deliverables are to be adhered to the most concurrent American National Standard: Standard for Maintenance Testing Specification for Electrical Power Equipment and Systems (ANSI/NETA MTS) as well as the VHA Directive 1028. This can be found in section 7.1 and 7.14 in the SOW. Additional code requirements can also be found in this section.

title: J061--Triennial Circuit Breaker and Feeder Testing
description: 1. VAAR 852.219-75 in the solicitation has box (iii), special trade construction contractors (75 percent), marked, while the requirement is coded J061 under NAICS 238210 and FAR 52.219-14 is also included. Please confirm that the 75 percent special trade limitation in box (iii) is the limitation that applies to this award. Confirmed. This requirement is solicited under NAICS 238210. The applicable limitation on subcontracting is VAAR 852.219-75(c)(iii), 75 percent for special trade construction contractors. Offeror must comply with that limitation and submit the signed certificate. 2. The SAM.gov notice shows no set-aside, while the solicitation includes VAAR 852.219-73 (total set-aside for certified SDVOSBs). Please confirm that this requirement is a total SDVOSB set-aside. Confirmed. This is a total SDVOSB set-aside per VAAR 852.219-73 and SF1449 Block 10. NCO 21 will update the SAM.gov notice to reflect the set-aside. Offerors must be certified SDVOSB in SBA Veteran Small Business Certification at time of offer. 3. Section B.1 states that invoices are submitted upon Government inspection and acceptance. Will VA accept two invoices, one after acceptance of field testing and one after acceptance of the coordination study and final report? Yes, the VA will take two invoices. Station/contracting will review these invoices for approval. 4. Amendment 0001 added Attachment C27, Single-Line Schematics. Please confirm whether C27 and the Facility Single Line Diagram together define the full quantities to be tested (MV switches, MV cable runs and vaults, liquid-filled and dry-type transformers, circuit breakers 225A and above, and feeders), or provide an equipment list with counts. Please also identify the buildings covered by "Day 12 + TBD, new facilities since 2017." In the past, a copy of 1-line diagrams was updated with color coding of each test component and a sheet with all quantiles and locations. This should be done to ensure vendor and FMS understands what scope is. 5. For the coordination study and arc flash analysis, is the 2024 study model available to the contractor, and in what software? Is there a required software platform and CAD version for the deliverables? Yes. However, I was just informed that our 2020 circuit breaker testing is the performed format which we can provide. 6. Must the coordination study and arc flash analysis be sealed by a Professional Engineer, and if so, must the engineer be licensed in Nevada? Yes engineering seal is required. No, it does not need to be Nevada. In the past, the previous vendor has had an engineer on staff who did this. 7. Please confirm that the five years of experience in the Contractor Requirements section is verified as a responsibility matter after quotes, and that the quote itself consists of price, the signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, amendment acknowledgments, and the items listed in FAR 52.212-1(a). Confirmed. Contractor Requirements Para 7.3 [5-year experience] will be evaluated as part of responsibility per FAR 9.104 after quotes, not as part of technical acceptability. For quote submission, see FAR 52.212-1(a) as supplemented by Addendum: price on B.2 Schedule, signed SF1449 Block 30 if required, acknowledgment of amendments per B.1 Para 4, signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, and proof of SDVOSB certification status. See also 52.212-3 if not in SAM. 8. Will VA facility electricians perform switching for the outages, and will VA provide temporary power or generator support where emergency branch equipment is de-energized? It is preferred that be in the vendor s scope of work. But verbiage should state that it will be done with Electrical supervisor or designee s authority at time of switching. Vendor should be responsible for the switching of the medium voltage system (25KV). This would be the P/Q switch in Boiler plant yard, medium voltage switches, and transformers in/on the facility down stream from the P/Q switch. VA electricians may assist with switching for 600 volts and less to aid in the testing. This must be arranged in the presented schedule to ensure proper VA staff is available. 9. What is the anticipated award date and the targeted notice-to-proceed window, so offerors can hold test crews for the night schedule? Anticipated award is within 2-3 weeks after the 11/9/2026 due date, subject to evaluations. NTP is intended ASAP after award per SOW 8.1. Offerors should plan to start coordination within 1 week of NTP. We will not require crews to be held prior to NTP. 10. Will a site visit be offered before the quote due date, and if so, will attendance be optional? VA high encourages site visits to visit equipment types, locations, and quantities. This has not been a bidding mandate to attend, but is encouraged. 11. Is there a deadline for questions, and will answers be issued by amendment? Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers that affect the SOW or terms will be issued by formal amendment to all offerors. Administrative clarifications may be answered by email. 12. The quote submission method and address, and the question deadline. Quotes shall be submitted by email to alex.arter@va.gov. Quotes are due November 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM Pacific Time. File size: split emails if over 20MB. Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers affecting SOW/terms/pricing will be issued by formal amendment. 13. Whether a site visit at the Ioannis A. Lougaris VAMC (Reno) will be held, and its date. A site visit is planned. Attendance will be optional. Date/time and meeting location will be issued by amendment once coordinated with Engineering. Offerors are encouraged to attend to verify existing conditions. No energized work will be performed during the site visit. 14. Breaker and feeder quantities by voltage class (LV/MV), and whether protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in scope. From the previous tests. There are: 11 MV Switches 10 MV Transformers 477 Circuit Breakers 570 Feeder Cables 27 LV Transformers Protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in the scope. The arc-flash label updates are to have their associated room numbers on them and must be done with professional engravings (i.e. no hand drawn labels). 15. Planned outage windows, and whether shutdowns must be after hours or on weekends. Yes. Per SOW 8.6, Electrical Testing shall be performed during Off Hours - 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM, weekends, and federal holidays. Photography work shall be performed during Normal Hours (Mon-Fri 6AM-6PM). The sequencing in SOW 8.1 shall be used as the basis for pricing. Final outage windows will be coordinated with the COR 2 weeks in advance per SOW 8.7 to minimize impact to patient care. 16. Required standard and deliverables (for example, NETA MTS and VHA Directive 1028 reporting). The required standard and deliverables are to be adhered to the most concurrent American National Standard: Standard for Maintenance Testing Specification for Electrical Power Equipment and Systems (ANSI/NETA MTS) as well as the VHA Directive 1028. This can be found in section 7.1 and 7.14 in the SOW. Additional code requirements can also be found in this section.

title: Medtronic cardiovascular "procedural packages"
description: This is a sources sought notice. The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support is seeking sources capable of providing Medtronic cardiovascular "procedural packages". The "procedural package" includes the cardiovascular products and ancillary accessories (such as needles for entry and guidewire) that are necessary for the physician to perform the cardiovascular surgeries. The product mix that makes up the "procedural package" varies based on the individual needs of the patient. All products must be approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The products that make up the �procedural package� must be delivered Just-In-Time (JIT), Direct Vendor Delivery (DVD) and Consignment. Under the JIT delivery method, the Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) calls the manufacturer�s field representative who carries the products into the MTF just-in-time for the surgery. The manufacturer�s sales representative may bring many sizes and types of implants and other auxiliary products to the surgery along with the instrumentation sets. Under the DVD method an order for products is placed through ECAT and the products are delivered direct to the customer via any transportation carrier. Under the consignment method, a Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) will have the products that make up the procedural package consigned to their facility. At the request of the MTF�s, the manufacturer is required to have a qualified representative on site at the MTF�s within the timeframe specified by the facility necessary to meet their requirements. The manufacturer�s representative provides technical advice and guidance to the physicians before, during and after implantation. Furthermore, technical support is available twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a week. This is a Request For Information (RFI) and does not commit the U.S. Government to issue a solicitation, make an award or pay any costs associated with responding to this announcement. All submitted information shall remain with the U.S. Government and will not be returned. Your response to this RFI shall be submitted electronically in PDF format and emailed to kathleen.adamow-wandall@dla.mil

Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. QUALITY ASSURANCE

description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) Issuing Agency: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Belvoir Division Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE): PAE Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE ASA) Project Manager (PM): PM Expeditionary Energy and Sustainment Systems (PM E2S2) NAICS Code: 335999 (Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing) and 335313 (Switchgear and Switchboard Apparatus Manufacturing) PSC / FSC Code: 6150 (Miscellaneous Electric Power and Distribution Equipment) Classification Code: 61 (Electric wire, and power and distribution equipment) Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (Market Research under FAR Part 10) 1.0 DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.201(e) and FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 2.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND & SCOPE The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. 3.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. Vendor capability to conduct First Article Testing (FAT) and environmental testing per MIL-DTL-53126. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit cost for each item. The feasibility of small business set-asides (e.g., Total Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 4.0 SPECIFIC INFORMATION REQUESTED (VENDOR QUESTIONNAIRE) Interested vendors are requested to provide clear, detailed responses to the questions below. Generic corporate marketing brochures that do not directly address these technical and manufacturing questions will not be considered. Section A: Corporate & Business Information Company Profile: Provide Company History (years in business), Name, Address, Website, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under SAM.gov. Business Size Standards: State your business size (number of employees) and socio-economic status under NAICS 335999 and 335313. Specify if your firm is: Large Business Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) / 8(a) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB / EDWOSB) Role & Teaming Intent: Do you intend to respond to a solicitation as a Prime Contractor, Joint Venture / Teaming Partner, or Subcontractor? If teaming or subcontracting, describe proposed workshare allocations and your strategy to satisfy the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Workload: If your company is awarded the contract, will you be able to perform at least 50% (percent) of the work required in house? Relevant Corporate Experience and Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of recent, relevant efforts involving build-to-print manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of ruggedized electrical distribution equipment, cable assemblies, or comparable military hardware. For each example, identify the customer, period of performance, scope, quantities, contract value, and customer point of contact, if available. Limit each past-performance example to two pages. Section B: Build-to-Print Manufacturing & Technical Capabilities TDP & Specification Conformance: PDISE requires fabrication to Government TDPs without redesign. Describe your facility�s experience manufacturing ruggedized power distribution centers, electrical enclosures, and high-power tactical cables to Government drawings (ASME Y14.100 / MIL-STD-31000). Tooling & Production Processes: Describe your capabilities for: Heavy-gauge multi-conductor power cable assembly. Assembly and wiring of circuit breaker inside distribution enclosures. Integration of MIL-DTL-22992 (Class L) heavy-duty cylindrical connectors into enclosures and cabling. Facilities and Production Control: Describe the availability, size, and location of facilities; manufacturing equipment; production capacity; production-control processes; records-management practices; and reporting systems used to support cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC): PDISE enclosures require pre-treatment and painting conforming to MIL-DTL-53072 and SAE-AMS-STD-595. Does your facility possess in-house CARC painting capabilities or do you rely on qualified third-party coating vendors? Packaging & Wood Packaging Material (WPM): Can your facility provide military preservation, marking, and crating conforming to Drawings 13230E7021/7020/7019? Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL): What is your current assessed Manufacturing Readiness Level for this class of tactical electrical distribution hardware? In-Process and Final Inspection: Describe your processes for receiving inspection of components and materials, in-process inspection, final inspection, nonconformance control, and documentation of inspection of completed PDISE or similar end items, as applicable. Section C: First Article Testing (FAT) & Environmental Qualification In-House vs. Subcontracted Testing: PDISE First Article Preproduction Inspection (FAT) requires 2 units per configuration tested within 180�360 Days After Contract Award (DACA). Identify whether your company possesses internal testing facilities or an established relationship with a DoD-certified laboratory to conduct First Article Testing in accordance with MIL-DTL-53126. title: USSS Construction Management & Engineering Services
description: Request for Information Construction Management Services NAICS Code 541330, Engineering Services Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI) Agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Secret Service (USSS) Response Due Date: November 20, 2026 Point of Contact: Kimberly Johnson, Contracting Officer, Assistant Division Chief, Office of Procurement 1. Purpose The U.S. Secret Service is conducting market research to identify qualified construction management firms capable of supporting future construction, renovation, design-management, and related task-order requirements. This Request for Information is issued solely for planning and market research purposes. USSS is seeking information from firms operating under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541330, Engineering Services, including small businesses and socioeconomic small-business concerns, that possess the organizational capacity, technical expertise, security capability, and geographic reach necessary to support future construction activities. Responses to this RFI will assist USSS in assessing industry capability, the availability of qualified firms, small-business participation, competition, bonding capacity, staffing resources, geographic coverage, and potential acquisition approaches for a future BPA or IDIQ type contract with the USSS. This RFI is not a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment, or promise by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. 2. Anticipated Requirement Description The U.S. Secret Service (USSS) anticipates a nationwide requirement for construction management and related design, engineering, security, infrastructure, and maintenance services at Government-owned or leased facilities and other Government-designated locations throughout the United States and its territories. Work may include new construction, renovations, retrofits, system upgrades, emergency repairs, and sustainment activities performed in occupied, operational, secure, or time-sensitive environments. Depending on the task order, firms may be required to provide services across the full project lifecycle, including: Planning, requirements development, site surveys, existing-condition assessments, project scoping, and cost estimating. Architectural and engineering design management, design review, value engineering, constructability review, and preparation of procurement-ready design documents. Acquisition and preconstruction support, including bid evaluation and contractor-vetting assistance. Construction administration and management, including quality control, safety and schedule oversight, stakeholder coordination, phased work, and management of design changes. Equipment procurement, fabrication, installation, systems integration, testing, commissioning, documentation, training, maintenance, repair, and urgent-response support, as specified in individual task orders. Anticipated task orders may cover one or more of the following service areas: Physical security enhancements: Perimeter controls, security booths and command posts, vehicle and pedestrian access points, site improvements, structural hardening, ballistic or blast-resistant features, secure rooms, doors, gates, locks, and related protective measures. Electronic security systems: Video surveillance and management, intrusion detection, access control, command-and-control, intercom and notification systems, supporting networks and equipment, system programming, cybersecurity hardening, integration, testing, and operator training. Infrastructure and building systems: Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, communications, emergency power, structured and fiber-optic cabling, fire and life-safety systems, HVAC, environmental controls, and building-management or monitoring platforms needed to support security and mission continuity. Preventive and corrective maintenance: Inspection, testing, calibration, software and firmware maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, component replacement, emergency response, spare-parts support, lifecycle assessment, and documentation for covered systems and infrastructure. The scope is broad and non-exhaustive. Each task order may establish the applicable locations, technical requirements, deliverables, performance standards, schedule, security restrictions, acceptance criteria, and maintenance obligations. Firms may need to integrate new, existing, legacy, or proprietary systems while minimizing disruption and maintaining safety, security, and continuity of operations. The Government anticipates that some future requirements may involve concurrent task orders of significant value. Respondents should identify their capacity to manage multiple projects simultaneously, including their ability to provide appropriately cleared personnel when required. 3. Industry Information Requested Interested firms are requested to complete and submit the attached Interested Vendor Questionnaire, U.S. Secret Service Construction Management Services, Request for Information, along with the supporting information identified below. 4. Submission Requirements Interested firms should submit the following: A completed Interested Vendor Questionnaire. A capability statement of no more than three pages. Information for up to three relevant completed projects from the past three years. Supporting project documentation, as available. Evidence of SAM.gov registration and applicable socioeconomic certifications, if requested or applicable. Responses should be submitted electronically in searchable PDF format to Kimberly Johnson, email: kimberly.m.johnson@usss.dhs.gov no later than November 20, 2026, 4:00 pm Eastern Standard time. The email subject line should read: RFI Response: USSS Construction Management Services � [Company Name] 5. Additional Information Respondents are encouraged to identify any recommended acquisition, contract-structure, ordering, scope-management, or small-business participation considerations that may help USSS develop a future requirement. Responses should not include sensitive operational, security, proprietary, or controlled information unless specifically authorized by applicable submission instructions. Firms should clearly mark proprietary information submitted in response to this RFI. The Government may use information received in response to this RFI to refine its acquisition strategy, determine the appropriate small-business approach, establish anticipated contract requirements, and develop any future solicitation. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation or award a contract because of this RFI. 6. RFI Disclaimer This RFI is for market research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment by the Government. Submission of a response is voluntary and will not result in reimbursement of any costs incurred. A response to this RFI is not required to participate in any future solicitation, should one be issued. title: Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) Issuing Agency: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Belvoir Division Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE): PAE Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE ASA) Project Manager (PM): PM Expeditionary Energy and Sustainment Systems (PM E2S2) NAICS Code: 335999 (Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing) and 335313 (Switchgear and Switchboard Apparatus Manufacturing) PSC / FSC Code: 6150 (Miscellaneous Electric Power and Distribution Equipment) Classification Code: 61 (Electric wire, and power and distribution equipment) Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (Market Research under FAR Part 10) 1.0 DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.201(e) and FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 2.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND & SCOPE The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. 3.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. Vendor capability to conduct First Article Testing (FAT) and environmental testing per MIL-DTL-53126. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit cost for each item. The feasibility of small business set-asides (e.g., Total Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 4.0 SPECIFIC INFORMATION REQUESTED (VENDOR QUESTIONNAIRE) Interested vendors are requested to provide clear, detailed responses to the questions below. Generic corporate marketing brochures that do not directly address these technical and manufacturing questions will not be considered. Section A: Corporate & Business Information Company Profile: Provide Company History (years in business), Name, Address, Website, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under SAM.gov. Business Size Standards: State your business size (number of employees) and socio-economic status under NAICS 335999 and 335313. Specify if your firm is: Large Business Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) / 8(a) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB / EDWOSB) Role & Teaming Intent: Do you intend to respond to a solicitation as a Prime Contractor, Joint Venture / Teaming Partner, or Subcontractor? If teaming or subcontracting, describe proposed workshare allocations and your strategy to satisfy the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Workload: If your company is awarded the contract, will you be able to perform at least 50% (percent) of the work required in house? Relevant Corporate Experience and Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of recent, relevant efforts involving build-to-print manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of ruggedized electrical distribution equipment, cable assemblies, or comparable military hardware. For each example, identify the customer, period of performance, scope, quantities, contract value, and customer point of contact, if available. Limit each past-performance example to two pages. Section B: Build-to-Print Manufacturing & Technical Capabilities TDP & Specification Conformance: PDISE requires fabrication to Government TDPs without redesign. Describe your facility�s experience manufacturing ruggedized power distribution centers, electrical enclosures, and high-power tactical cables to Government drawings (ASME Y14.100 / MIL-STD-31000). Tooling & Production Processes: Describe your capabilities for: Heavy-gauge multi-conductor power cable assembly. Assembly and wiring of circuit breaker inside distribution enclosures. Integration of MIL-DTL-22992 (Class L) heavy-duty cylindrical connectors into enclosures and cabling. Facilities and Production Control: Describe the availability, size, and location of facilities; manufacturing equipment; production capacity; production-control processes; records-management practices; and reporting systems used to support cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC): PDISE enclosures require pre-treatment and painting conforming to MIL-DTL-53072 and SAE-AMS-STD-595. Does your facility possess in-house CARC painting capabilities or do you rely on qualified third-party coating vendors? Packaging & Wood Packaging Material (WPM): Can your facility provide military preservation, marking, and crating conforming to Drawings 13230E7021/7020/7019? Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL): What is your current assessed Manufacturing Readiness Level for this class of tactical electrical distribution hardware? In-Process and Final Inspection: Describe your processes for receiving inspection of components and materials, in-process inspection, final inspection, nonconformance control, and documentation of inspection of completed PDISE or similar end items, as applicable. Section C: First Article Testing (FAT) & Environmental Qualification In-House vs. Subcontracted Testing: PDISE First Article Preproduction Inspection (FAT) requires 2 units per configuration tested within 180�360 Days After Contract Award (DACA). Identify whether your company possesses internal testing facilities or an established relationship with a DoD-certified laboratory to conduct First Article Testing in accordance with MIL-DTL-53126. title: CFLHD Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) for Architect-Engineer Design Services
description: Architect and Engineering (A-E) Services The Federal Highway Administration, Central Federal Lands Highway Division (CFLHD), anticipates soliciting and awarding multiple Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for A-E services with a partial small business set-aside. CFLHD provides engineering and construction services on projects in the states of Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming on behalf of Federal Land Management Agencies and other Agencies. These Agencies include: the National Park Service (NPS); USDA Forest Service (Forest Service); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS); Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) and Tribal Governments; Bureau of Land Management (BLM); Department of Defense (DOD); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE); and the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR). The shared capacity of the IDIQs will be $60 million. The acquisition will be solicited and awarded on a competitive basis and is being made under the North America Industry Classification Code 541330 and is open to all business concerns. The planned duration for the contracts is a total of five years. Projects are typically located in environmentally sensitive areas that necessitate context-sensitive design techniques and processes. Project topography type and climatic zones vary greatly including coastal, mountainous, desert and plains regions. Projects will primarily involve improvements to low-volume and low-speed roadways ranging from 3R (resurfacing, restoration and rehabilitation) to full reconstruction. The geographic jurisdiction of CFLHD includes, but is not limited to, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming.

title: Z1DA--642-22-104 | Upgrade Substation Building 2 Phase 1 for Philadelphia VAMC
description: 642-22-104, 36C24426R0088, Upgrade Substation Building 2, Phase 1, PHL CMCVAMC Proposal Due Date: 11/20/2026 at 4:00pm EST. Email proposals to Kevin Rodgers at kevin.rodgers2@va.gov. Corporal Michael J. Crescenz Medical Center (CMC VAMC) requires replacement of Electrical Substations 1 and 2 in order to increase electrical capacity to support future facility projects. The existing substations are approximately 29 years old and require replacement to support current and future electrical demands. This project will replace Electrical Substations 1 and 2 with new 480/277V substations each containing a 1500 kVA transformer. A temporary 480/277V substation with a 1500 kVA transformer shall be installed to maintain electrical service to the facility during demolition and construction activities. Upon completion of construction, the temporary substation shall remain installed as a spare substation for the facility. All work shall be phased to minimize service outages and maintain continuous operation of the medical center. Defined and issued bid documents (drawings and specifications) will serve as the basis of this construction project.

title: Z1DA--642-22-104 | Upgrade Substation Building 2 Phase 1 for Philadelphia VAMC
description: 642-22-104, 36C24426R0088, Upgrade Substation Building 2, Phase 1, PHL CMCVAMC Proposal Due Date: 11/20/2026 at 4:00pm EST. Email proposals to Kevin Rodgers at kevin.rodgers2@va.gov. Corporal Michael J. Crescenz Medical Center (CMC VAMC) requires replacement of Electrical Substations 1 and 2 in order to increase electrical capacity to support future facility projects. The existing substations are approximately 29 years old and require replacement to support current and future electrical demands. This project will replace Electrical Substations 1 and 2 with new 480/277V substations each containing a 1500 kVA transformer. A temporary 480/277V substation with a 1500 kVA transformer shall be installed to maintain electrical service to the facility during demolition and construction activities. Upon completion of construction, the temporary substation shall remain installed as a spare substation for the facility. All work shall be phased to minimize service outages and maintain continuous operation of the medical center. Defined and issued bid documents (drawings and specifications) will serve as the basis of this construction project.

title: Sniper Comprehensive Advanced Targeting Pod (CATP2) Support and Sustainment Option Years 6 & 7
description: This solicitation is issued with the intent of awarding Sniper CATP2 Option Years 6 & 7. The contractor shall provide efforts required for the management, engineering, production, fabrication, integration, Configuration Management (CM), test, test support, hardware and software upgrades, resolution of Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS), and logistics support of the Sniper system to ensure a system availability rate and reliability Mean Time Between Maintenance Events (MTBME). The Contractor shall adhere to Contractor Quality System; ensuring it is an integral and integrated part of the Contractor's complete management system. The contract period of performance will be for two one-year options, and the Government intends to negotiate and award sole source to Lockheed Martin Corporation (CAGE 04939), 5600 West Sand Lake Road, Orlando FL 32819, in accordance with Revolutionary Far Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement of proposal, which shall be reviewed by the U.S. Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. In accordance with Air Force Instruction (AFI) 16-201, foreign participation is not permitted at the prime contract level. All potential offerors should contact the Contract Specialist/Procuring Contracting Officer for additional information, questions, and/or concerns. Place of performance will be at Robins Air Force Base, GA, or at contractor or subcontractor facilities. Interested Party of Person(s) may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit a proposal(s). This solicitation is not a request for competitive proposals. All proposals received within the 15 days after issuance of solicitation will be considered. The purpose of the Ombudsman is not to diminish the authority of the program director or contracting officer, but to communicate serious Contractor concern, issues, disagreements, and recommendations to appropriate government personnel. When requested, the Ombudsman will maintain strict confidentiality as to the source of the concern. The Ombudsman does not participate in the evaluation of proposals or in the source selection process. When appropriate potential offeror(s) may contract Nicole Furlough at nicole.furlough@us.af.mil or 478-222-1088. Please be prepared to identify previous contacts made by you in an attempt to resolve your concerns.

title: AMS Designated Laboratory Meat Testing Services (ADL)
description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is issuing Solicitation 12?1NTS?26?R?0002 to obtain proposals from responsible, accredited analytical laboratories to perform microbiological and fat testing in support of AMS meat, poultry, egg, and aquatic product procurement programs. This requirement establishes AMS Designated Laboratories (ADLs) responsible for conducting all required microbiological and chemical analyses on samples submitted by AMS vendors, ensuring compliance with Federal Purchase Program Specifications (FPPS) and supporting food safety and quality verification efforts. AMS intends to award an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) firm?fixed?price contract, consisting of a Base Period and up to four option periods, covering performance from April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2032. Offerors must be fully capable of meeting all technical, accreditation, reporting, and quality assurance requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW) and must maintain ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for all applicable microbiological and chemical test methods throughout the contract term. Offerors are required to submit a complete proposal package in accordance with Section E of the solicitation, including all technical, management, past performance, and pricing components, as well as a properly completed and signed SF?1449. Offerors must ensure all requirements, instructions, and submission details�such as WBSCM electronic submission processes�are fully reviewed and followed. Incomplete proposals may not be considered for award. Key expectations under this solicitation include: � Performance of all required microbiological and fat analyses using approved methods (FSIS MLG, AOAC, AOCS, or AMS?approved alternatives). � Comprehensive sample preparation, receipt, testing, reporting, and data management in accordance with AMS SOW requirements. � Timely reporting of results, including notification of presumptive or confirmed pathogen positives to AMS, FSIS, and vendors. � Secure handling and management of proprietary AMS data. � Full compliance with FAR, AGAR, and USDA?specific contract clauses incorporated into the solicitation. Prospective offerors are strongly encouraged to read the entire solicitation package, including the SOW, exhibits, and all referenced clauses, to ensure a complete and conforming submission.

This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 70Z03826RB0000006 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) effective as of November 28, 2025. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 336413. The small business size standard is 1,250 employees. This is being solicited on a sole source basis. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which shall be considered by the agency. The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Aviation Logistics Center (ALC), Elizabeth City, NC intends to award an Indefinite Delivery Requirements type contract to BAE Systems Land & Armaments, L.P. (BAE) of Phoenix, AZ. This requirement will be solicited on an other than full and open competition basis under the authority of FAR 12.102 (b) for the procurement of spare parts for the pilot, co-pilot, and mechanic aircraft seats on the MH-65E Aircraft. BAE (Cage Code 54786) is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the only distributor source in North America capable of providing the required parts in the Schedule. The contract will consist of a one-year base period and if exercised, up to four (4) one-year option periods. This contract shall not exceed five (5) years. See the following attached documents titled: �Attachment 1 � Schedule of Supplies 70Z03826RB0000006�, �Attachment 2 � Provisions, Clauses, and Terms and Conditions 70Z03826RB0000006�, and �Attachment 3 - Redacted J and A � 70Z03826RB0000006�. Concerns having the expertise and required capabilities to provide these items are invited to submit offers in accordance with the requirements stipulated in this solicitation. Parts must be approved in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) guidelines to ensure safety of our aircrew. The Government shall ensure all procurements are awarded without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. Only the use of airworthy commercial specifications or standard military specifications/military standard parts will be utilized and approved from this solicitation. Newly manufactured commercial items will only be procured from sources able to provide a Certificate of Conformance (COC) and traceability to the OEM. The Federal Aviation Regulation, Part 21, outlines certification procedures. The contractor shall furnish a Certificate of Conformance (COC) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.246-15. Certificate of conformance must be submitted in the format specified in the clause. All parts shall be NEW approved parts. Offerors must be able to provide necessary certification including traceability to the manufacturer, manufacturer's COC and its own COC to ensure parts are in airworthy condition, suitable for installation on USCG aircraft. Prospective vendors who are not the OEM or an authorized distributor must provide traceability for the offered product back to the manufacturer or authorized distributor. Traceability means a clear, complete, documented, and auditable paper trail which traces each step from an OEM or distributor to its current location. Traceability to the OEM must have only two exchanges prior to USCG delivery. Alternate parts will not be authorized. NO SUBSTITUTE PARTS WILL BE CONSIDERED. ONLY NEW PARTS WILL BE ACCEPTED. The Government reserves the right to withhold any item or group of items contained in this solicitation upon award. The Government reserves the right to make a single award, to make multiple awards covering different subsets of CLINs, or to make no award. The Government shall assume, for the purpose of making multiple awards, that $500 would be the administrative cost to the Government for issuing and administering each contract awarded under this solicitation. Individual awards shall be for the items or combinations of items that result in the lowest cost to the Government including the assumed administrative costs. The government shall ensure all procurements are awarded without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. NOTE: NO DRAWINGS, SPECIFICATIONS OR SCHEMATICS ARE AVAILABLE FROM THIS AGENCY. Closing date and time for receipt of offers is 9 March 2026 at 4:30 pm EDT. Any quotation received after the closing date and time specified are considered late. E-mailed quotations are required and shall be sent to Livia.M.Pippen@uscg.mil. Please indicate solicitation 70Z03826RB0000006 in the subject line. Phone call quotations WILL NOT be accepted.

Красного маяка, д. 17, к.3;Осигуряване на незабавна реакция на моторизиран екип на сигнали за тревога, подавани от паник-бутоните;Поддръжка на техническото състояние на средствата за сигнализация;Поддръжка и ремонт на две системи за видеонаблюдение, инсталирани в административната сграда на ЦПРБ на адрес: Москва, ул.
